text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures surged to new contract highs in late dealings, buoyed by a firmer U.S. debt market and buying spurred by the Federal Reserve not raising short-term interest rates. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 98.74, up 0.57 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts raced ahead in the afternoon session, chasing U.S. Treasuries which rallied from the open as several big players weighed in with massive buy orders. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-0/32, up 17/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French 10-year bond yields fell to their lowest level since February 24, 1994 as debt markets took comfort from the decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 124.52, up 0.40 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets soared to new heights, boosted by lira strength against the mark, as the conviction grew that a tough budget will generate enough momentum to carry Italy into a currency union by 1999. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 120.29, up 1.12 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Prices of U.S. Treasury securities traded higher across the maturities spectrum at midday, as reported central bank buying buoyed prices. Dealers pointed to central bank buying in two- and three-year securities earlier this morning, followed by another bout of purchases in two- and five-year notes as the midday hour approached. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-6/32, up 18/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.94 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures rose, following the Fed's decision overnight to leave interest rates unchanged, but gains were pared on hedge sales after a JGB auction. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.25, down 0.15 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market volumes rocketed as bond markets rallied after U.S. interest rates were left unchanged at yesterday's FOMC meeting. The dollar sector saw over $2.0 billion of new supply including JR East's expected $800 million 10-year deal. In marks, the IADB set a 500 million mark 10-year benchmark issue and LB Rheinland-Pfalz issued a 1.0 billion mark seven-year bond. CADES will launch a 12 billion French franc July 2005 bond on Thursday at 5-7 b.p. over OATs.
